subject.title: Active Memory + Codex app-server path causes long response latency, hook timeouts, startup aborts, and gateway event-loop stalls

question: Should Active Memory retain embedded-agent recall as its supported default and receive targeted isolation fixes, or should maintainers sponsor a new lightweight single-shot/nonblocking recall mode for latency-sensitive use?
rationale: The reports establish an existing reliability bug, but the durable architecture choice changes plugin behavior, provider/runtime coupling, and potentially configuration surface; automation should not choose that policy unilaterally.

options.title: Adopt isolated lightweight recall
options.body: Sponsor a bounded one-shot or nonblocking recall path for latency-sensitive pre-prompt use, with explicit compatibility and quality tests.

options.title: Harden embedded recall only
options.body: Keep the existing recall model, but exclude helper sessions and isolate or cancel it so it cannot block parent runs or delivery.

options.title: Split the work
options.body: Track the helper-session eligibility defect separately while retaining this issue for the broader Codex and embedded-runtime reliability decision.

recommendation.title: Adopt isolated lightweight recall
recommendation.body: Sponsor a bounded one-shot or nonblocking recall path for latency-sensitive pre-prompt use, with explicit compatibility and quality tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned routing point for the related Active Memory reliability issue covering the same pre-prompt blocking behavior.
